steps.title: Sacrifice mouse and harvest intestine
steps.instruction: Euthanize one Lgr5‑EGFP‑IRES‑creERT2 mouse according to institutional IACUC guidelines (max 4 mice per run). Dissect out the entire small intestine, leaving out the final 5 cm of ileum, and place immediately in ice‑cold PBS in a Petri dish.

steps.title: Open intestine and rinse
steps.instruction: Longitudinally open the intestine with scissors in ice‑cold PBS, transfer to a 50 mL conical tube containing 15 mL ice‑cold PBS and invert the tube 15 times to remove visible debris.

steps.title: Cut tissue and first EDTA wash
steps.instruction: Cut the intestine into ~5 mm pieces, transfer to 10 mL ice‑cold 5 mM EDTA‑PBS, shake vigorously for 15 s, then let fragments settle by gravity for 30 s.

steps.title: First EDTA incubation (10 min)
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the fragments, add 10 mL fresh 5 mM EDTA‑PBS and place the tube on a benchtop roller at 4 °C (speed 2.5) for 10 min.

steps.title: Second EDTA incubation (30 min)
steps.instruction: Repeat the previous step: aspirate supernatant, add 10 mL fresh 5 mM EDTA‑PBS, and incubate at 4 °C on the roller for 30 min.

steps.title: Wash crypts and collect fractions
steps.instruction: Allow fragments to settle on ice, aspirate supernatant, add 10 mL cold PBS, shake vigorously for 15 s and collect the supernatant as Fraction 1 (discard – villus‑rich). Add another 10 mL cold PBS, shake 15 s and collect as Fraction 2. Repeat the PBS wash and collection three more times to obtain Fractions 3‑5.

steps.title: Filter and centrifuge crypt fractions
steps.instruction: Coat a 50 mL tube with 1 % PBS‑BSA by vigorous shaking. Filter the pooled Fractions 2‑5 through a 70 µm cell strainer into the coated tube, then centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. Aspirate the supernatant; keep the pellet on ice.

steps.title: Enzymatic dissociation with TrypLE
steps.instruction: Resuspend the crypt pellet in 1.0 mL TrypLE Express containing 100 µL DNase I (use a 2 mL pipette), keep on ice, then incubate in a 37 °C water bath for 5 min. Immediately return the tube to ice.

steps.title: Neutralize and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Add 12 mL ice‑cold MEMα, mix gently by pipetting up and down twice with a 10 mL pipette, then centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. Aspirate the supernatant while keeping the pellet on ice.

steps.title: Antibody staining on ice
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 0.5 mL ice‑cold MEMα containing Pacific Blue‑conjugated CD24, APC‑conjugated CD31, and APC‑conjugated CD45 antibodies each at 1 / 500 dilution. Incubate on ice for 15 min (prepare basal medium in parallel).

steps.title: Wash, filter and second centrifugation
steps.instruction: Add 12 mL MEMα, triturate the pellet, filter through a 70 µm cell strainer into a 50 mL tube, transfer to a 15 mL tube and centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. Aspirate supernatant while preparing basal medium containing 1.5 µM propidium iodide (PI).

steps.title: PI staining and final filtration
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 1.5 mL basal medium with 1.5 µM PI, filter through a 40 µm cell strainer into a 50 mL tube, then transfer the suspension to a FACS tube. (Clean and replace Pipet‑Aid filter frequently to avoid cell damage.)

steps.title: Prepare collection tubes for sorting
steps.instruction: Coat two 1.5 mL tubes with 500 µL 1 % PBS‑BSA (shake vigorously) and keep on ice; these will receive sorted Paneth cells and ISCs respectively.

steps.title: FACS sort Paneth cells and ISCs
steps.instruction: Using a BD FACS Aria III, sort Paneth cells (CD24^hi SideScatter^hi Lgr5‑EGFP⁻ CD31⁻ CD45⁻ PI⁻) and ISCs (Lgr5‑EGFP^hi CD24⁻ CD31⁻ CD45⁻ PI⁻) into the prepared collection tubes. Aim for 20,000–50,000 cells of each type per mouse. If sorting exceeds 1 h after dissociation, filter the sample again through a 40‑µm strainer before loading.

steps.title: Centrifuge sorted cells and adjust volume
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the collection tubes at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, aspirate supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in basal medium to a final volume of 30–100 µL (depending on cell count).

steps.title: Count cells and verify concentration
steps.instruction: Take 5 µL from each tube, load onto a hemocytometer, and count under a microscope. Adjust so that cell concentration is 1,000–2,000 cells/µL.

steps.title: Combine Paneth cells and ISCs
steps.instruction: On ice, mix 2,000 Paneth cells with 2,000 ISCs in a fresh 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Prepare organoid growth medium
steps.instruction: Make organoid growth medium as described in the Recipes (basal medium supplemented with 1 mM N‑acetylcysteine, 50 ng/mL EGF, 200 ng/mL Noggin, 1/30 R‑spondin‑1 conditioned medium, 3/100 Afamin/Wnt3a CM). Prepare fresh before use.

steps.title: Prepare Matrigel mixture with additives
steps.instruction: Dilute growth‑factor‑reduced Matrigel to 75 % (v/v) with organoid growth medium. Add JAG‑1 from 1 mM stock at 1 µM final concentration (1 / 1000 dilution) and Y‑27632 from 10 mM stock at 10 µM final concentration (1 / 1000 dilution). Mix gently.

steps.title: Embed cells in Matrigel drops
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL of the Matrigel‑cell mixture to a well of a 48‑well plate, gently mix, and allow the dome to solidify by incubating 10 min at 37 °C.

steps.title: Overlay with organoid growth medium
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL of freshly prepared organoid growth medium to each well, taking care not to disturb the solidified Matrigel. No medium change is required from day 1 to day 5.

steps.title: Incubate and assess colony formation
steps.instruction: Culture the plate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. On day 5, count the number of colonies with a lumen under a microscope (use at least two technical replicates for reliable quantification).
